system:
You write a short household emergency SOP in markdown for a family, so a spouse, teen, or sitter can act safely when the homeowner is away, using only the sources provided.
The body must contain exactly these four headings, in this order, and nothing else at heading level 2:
- ## Title and scope
- ## Steps
- ## Escalation criteria
- ## Do not
Steps are numbered, short, and imperative.
Put people's safety first: get everyone to safety, then stop the source at a shutoff or breaker, then call for help, then limit damage.
For a gas smell or CO alarm, tell the reader to leave first and call 911 or the gas utility from outside; do not touch light switches, appliances, or the gas meter unless the sources say to.
Never tell the reader to repair gas, electrical, or HVAC equipment. Go no further than closing a shutoff, resetting a breaker once, or cleanup.
Refer to the household's own shutoffs, valves, and numbers generically (for example "see House facts"); never guess where they are.
Escalation criteria say when to call 911 or the gas or utility emergency line and when to get everyone out.
The "Do not" section lists common mistakes.
Cite only facts found in the sources.
Do not add a Sources section; the app renders it.
prompt:
Protocol title: Gas smell or CO alarm

Sources:

### https://gas-safety.example/gas-leak — What to do if you smell gas
What to do if you smell gas

If you smell gas, leave the house right away. Take everyone with you, including pets.

Do not turn lights or appliances on or off, do not use a phone or open a garage door inside the house, and do not try to find the leak.

Once you are outside and away from the building, call 911 or your gas utility's emergency line.

Do not go back inside until the gas utility or the fire department says it is safe. Only a qualified technician should repair gas pipes or appliances.
raw:
{"bodyMd":"## Title and scope
Gas smell or CO alarm: what a family member or sitter does when the home may have a gas leak or carbon monoxide.

## Steps
1. Leave the house right away and take everyone, including pets.
2. From outside, call 911 or the gas utility emergency line.
3. For the location of the gas shutoff and the utility number, see House facts.
4. Stay outside until the gas utility or fire department says it is safe.

## Escalation criteria
- Call 911 for any gas smell, CO alarm, or anyone feeling dizzy or sick.
- Get everyone out first; call from outside.

## Do not
- Do not turn lights or appliances on or off.
- Do not go back inside before the utility or fire department says it is safe.
- Do not try to repair gas pipes or appliances."}
